bayes.prior: Beta(1,1) flat prior in the numeric fields; Beta(50,50) (100 pseudo-draws at 0.5) computed in parallel and reported in results.json and in this summary
bayes.summary: 656 draws, 7216 ball slots. Per-number counts range 299 (no. 13) to 350 (nos. 7 and 15); null mean 328. Beta(1,1) posterior means 0.456-0.533; 95% intervals: only no. 13 excludes 0.5 ([0.418,0.494]), nos. 7/15 are [0.495,0.571]; one of 22 intervals missing 0.5 is exactly what 22 independent-looking tests produce at 5%. P(p_n>0.5): min 0.012 (no. 13), max 0.957 (nos. 7, 15). Beta(50,50) shrinks to 0.462-0.529 and P(p>0.5) 0.017-0.945 (CI for no. 13 then [0.426,0.497]). Dispersion test with the 11-of-22 covariance (Var=N/4, Cov=-N/84, so sum (c-N/2)^2/((N/4)(22/21)) ~ chi2_21): Q=21.70, p=0.417 analytic, 0.452 by 500-history Monte Carlo - the spread of counts is exactly what uniform draws give. Hierarchical method of moments: sample variance of rates 4.125e-4 vs null expectation 3.992e-4 (MC 4.03e-4) -> tau^2=1.33e-5, tau=0.0036, i.e. true inclusion rates differ by at most ~0.4 percentage points around 0.5 and even that is within the sampling noise of tau itself. Bayes factors for 'all p_n=0.5' vs free rates: product-binomial Beta(1,1) marginal likelihood (variance-correct) 8.1e23 (log10 23.9); Beta(50,50) 2.5e5; Dirichlet-multinomial on ball slots alpha=1: 5.3e24, alpha=0.5: 3.7e28, alpha=50: 1.2e7; BIC approximation with n=656 draws 4.3e24 (with n=7216 slots 1.1e38). Every variant is decisive for the uniform model. Implication for picking numbers: the posterior ranking is noise. Even taking the Beta(1,1) posterior means literally and playing the 11 highest (7,15,19,16,3,17,1,8,5,21,22) would multiply the jackpot probability by only 1.22 (1/352716 -> about 1/288000) under a conditional-Bernoulli model, and the walk-forward 'long-run frequency' ticket shows that ranking does not even persist out of sample (5.504 hits/draw vs 5.5). No number deserves preference; the complement symmetry means the 'cold' ticket is equally (un)attractive.

entropy.summary: Shannon entropy of the empirical number distribution 4.45829 bits vs log2(22)=4.45943; the 0.0011-bit deficit equals the finite-sample deficit of uniform histories (500-history MC mean 4.45832, sd 0.00034, z=-0.08). Compression of the 656x22 incidence matrix packed to 1804 bytes: zlib(9) ratio 1.00610 observed, simulated 1.00610 +- 0.0 (z=0; degenerate because zlib/lzma emit incompressible input as stored blocks with fixed overhead, lzma 1.0333 likewise identical for all histories); the informative variants are bz2 1.2373 vs 1.2192 +- 0.0087 (z=+2.08, observed LESS compressible than 99% of uniform histories) and zlib on the sorted numbers-as-bytes encoding (7216 bytes) 0.4020 vs 0.3988 +- 0.0017 (z=+1.86, also less compressible). No compressor finds structure. Serial test: overlap of consecutive draws vs Hypergeometric(22,11,11) in bins <=3,4,5,6,7,>=8: chi2=4.54 on 5 df, p=0.474 (MC p=0.456); mean lag-1 overlap 5.565 vs 5.5 (z=+1.38); lag 1..10 overlap z-scores +1.38,+0.46,+1.03,-0.36,-0.28,-1.27,-0.51,+1.54,+1.88,+0.46 (none significant after 10 lags); lag-1 conditional entropy H(X_t|X_t-1)=0.99990 bits, mutual information 0.0001 bits, P(1|1)=0.506, P(1|0)=0.494. Other diagnostics: Wald-Wolfowitz runs test aggregated over the 22 number series z=-1.42 (p=0.16), 0/22 numbers individually significant; sum of drawn numbers mean 127.1 vs 126.5 (z=+0.45); even-count mean 5.41 vs 5.5 (z=-1.89, p=0.06); weekday x number association MC p=0.20; pooled gap distribution vs Geometric(1/2) chi2=4.81 on 5 df, p=0.44. All axes are consistent with i.i.d. uniform 11-of-22 draws.

ml.model: Per-number ridge logistic regression (numpy Newton/IRLS, L2=1 on standardized features): lags 1..7 of the number's 0/1 series, rolling frequency over last 30 and 90 draws, current gap, day-of-week one-hot (17 features + intercept); walk-forward on draws t=200..655 (0-based), refit every 20 draws (23 refits) using only draws < refit time; random tie-break; Monte-Carlo null (4000 sims) conditional on the prediction sequence
ml.summary: Per-number LR is WORSE than the coin-flip baseline out of sample: log-loss 0.7371 vs ln2=0.6931 (paired per-draw t=+12.1 in the wrong direction; MC p that a null draw sequence would give an equal or lower log-loss = 0.22), Brier 0.2680 vs 0.25, AUC 0.5065 (MC p=0.12). It is badly overconfident: predicted deciles 0.26 -> observed 0.49, 0.75 -> observed 0.51; predicted probabilities span 0.015-0.988 with no corresponding signal. Its top-11 ticket scored 5.564 hits/draw vs 5.5 (z=+1.13, p=0.26 normal, 0.24 MC) and produced FEWER extreme outcomes (<=3 or >=8 hits) than chance: 0.0768 vs 0.0861 (35 of 456 draws; MC p=0.79), hits histogram 2:2,3:15,4:64,5:143,6:126,7:88,8:17,9:1, never 0/1/10/11. Stronger ridge (L2=10): log-loss 0.7145, hits 5.546 (z=0.82), extreme 0.0724. Pooled LR (shared coefficients): log-loss 0.6944, AUC 0.491, hits 5.496, extreme 0.1075 (MC p=0.07). Markov lag-1 per number: log-loss 0.6957, AUC 0.499, hits 5.478. Pooled gap-hazard ('due' numbers): log-loss 0.6938, hits 5.546 (tie-break average 5.489). Hot-30 rule: hits 5.393 (z=-1.91, p=0.056), its exact complement cold-30: 5.607 (same |z|, extreme 0.0680) - the smallest p among all tests. Hot-90: 5.456; long-run frequency: 5.504. Random-ticket baseline (2000 random tickets per draw vs real outcomes): 5.5017 hits, extreme 0.0861; the SD of mean hits across 4000 one-random-ticket-per-draw strategies is 0.0557 vs theory 1.2002/sqrt(456)=0.0562, validating the z formula. Holm-Bonferroni over 45 model x metric tests: min raw p=0.056, min adjusted p=1.0. If the per-number LR probabilities were literally true the top ticket's jackpot odds would be 50x better (median 23x) - but those probabilities are refuted by the out-of-sample log-loss; under the pooled LR the implied multiplier is 1.19 and under the static posterior-mean ticket 1.22. Realised predictive power: none.

diag.overall: The 656-draw history (01.01.2025-19.10.2026, one empty row skipped, Dan column matches the dates, one 2-day calendar gap) is statistically indistinguishable from i.i.d. uniform 11-of-22 draws on every axis examined: marginal frequencies (chi2 dispersion p=0.42, hierarchical between-number SD 0.0036, Bayes factors of 1e5-1e24 for 'all rates = 0.5' depending on prior), Shannon entropy (z=-0.08 vs uniform histories), compressibility (no compressor beats the uniform-history reference; bz2 and byte encodings find the real data slightly LESS compressible), serial dependence (lag-1 overlap chi2 p=0.47, conditional entropy 0.99990 bits, lags 1-10 all |z|<1.9), runs, gaps, sums, parity and weekday effects. In strictly chronological walk-forward validation over 456 test draws, no predictor beats the random baseline: the per-number logistic regression is significantly WORSE than a coin flip (log-loss 0.737 vs 0.693, Brier 0.268 vs 0.25) because it fits noise, its AUC is 0.507, and its top-11 ticket scores 5.56 hits/draw (z=+1.1) with fewer extreme outcomes than chance (0.077 vs 0.086). Pooled LR, Markov lag-1, gap-hazard, hot/cold 30/90-draw and long-run frequency rules all land within noise (|z|<=1.9); the smallest raw p of 45 tests is 0.056 and the Holm-adjusted minimum is 1.0. Even the most charitable reading - taking the Beta(1,1) posterior means as true and playing the 11 highest - would raise the jackpot probability by a factor of 1.22 (1/352716 -> ~1/288000), moving the expected return of a 1.30 EUR ticket from 0.539 EUR (41.5%) to 0.590 EUR (45.4%) under the stated prize table, still a loss of more than half the stake; the realised out-of-sample edge is zero. predictive_power_found=false. best3.method: Exact. All 352716 candidate 11-subsets containing number 1 (the other 352716 are complements with identical prize sets) were evaluated exactly at every step: for the union U of the current portfolio, cnt(c)=#{d in U: |c&d| in H} was computed for ALL candidates simultaneously with two zeta transforms over the 2^22 lattice (N(S)=#{d in U: S subset d} by superset-sum; cnt(c)=sum_{S subset c} w(|S|)N(S) by subset-sum, w(s)=sum_{h in H}(-1)^(s-h)C(s,h)), verified against direct vectorised popcount (6294/244 for every candidate when U=all draws; 40 random candidates vs direct count at step 1; final 13-portfolio re-evaluated by direct popcount). Greedy 3 picks (gain = 6294 - overlap_all, tie-break 244 - overlap_hi, then lowest 22-bit mask), then coordinate-ascent swaps, each swap step exhaustive over all candidates; one full sweep found no improvement. Duplicates and complements of existing tickets excluded. Result 79932 = 61050 + 3*6294 equals the absolute upper bound (each ticket wins in exactly 6294 draws), so the triple is a certified global optimum for union_all; likewise union_hi 3172 = 2440 + 3*244 and union_jp 26 = 20 + 6 are the maxima. The optimum is highly non-unique: 1816 candidates have win sets fully disjoint from the 10-ticket union (gain 6294), 814019 pairs and 116006224 triples of them are mutually disjoint, and every such triple yields the identical 13-ticket payout distribution.
